note_text:
Patient is a 58-year-old woman referred by her primary care physician directly for urodynamic testing based on a phone call describing "leaking with coughing and urgency for several months." No prior office visit with this urology practice has occurred; patient was scheduled straight into the urodynamics suite today without an intake history and physical having been performed, and no urinalysis has been obtained.

On arrival, the technician confirms patient identity and reviews consent for the study. Patient reports she has had urinary leakage with laughing and sneezing, plus a sense of urgency and occasional urge incontinence, ongoing for approximately 6 months, and that she voids about 10-12 times a day. Beyond this brief verbal report obtained by the tech at check-in, no formal history was taken by a physician or advanced practice provider, no physical/pelvic exam was documented, and no urine sample was collected or analyzed prior to proceeding.

Multichannel urodynamic study performed: uroflowmetry, filling cystometry with intra-abdominal pressure monitoring, and pressure-flow voiding study. Study demonstrates involuntary detrusor contractions at 220 mL with associated urgency, and stress leak point pressure of 68 cm H2O with Valsalva. No obstruction pattern noted. Bladder capacity 410 mL.

Impression: Mixed urinary incontinence with detrusor overactivity and stress component. Plan: counsel patient on pelvic floor physical therapy and consider anticholinergic trial; results will be reviewed with the referring physician. Note: initial baseline history/physical exam and urinalysis with microscopy were not performed prior to this urodynamic study, as testing was scheduled directly from the referral without an antecedent clinic visit.
